title: SPA/93/2013 of NAVEEN CHANDRA GURURANI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 93 of 2013

Naveen Chandra Gururani
S/o Shri Madhwnand,
Present posted as Anushewak (Class 4th)
In the office of Chief Veterinary Office, Champawat,
District Champawat.
 Ö Appellant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand
Through Secretary, Animal Husbandry, Dehradun
And Others.
 Ö Respondents
Dr. Anil Dabral with Mr. MS Bisht, Advocates, present for the appellant.
Mr. KP Upadhyaya, CSC, for the respondents no. 1 & 2.
M
r. GD Joshi, Advocate, for the respondent no. 3.

Coram: Honíble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
 Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Per : Honíble Prafulla C. Pant, J. (ORAL)

Heard learned Counsel for the parties and
perused the papers on record.
2. This appeal is directed against the order
dated 22.3.2013, passed by a learned Single Judge of
this Court in Writ Petition No. 307/2013 (S/S),
whereby the said Court has dismissed the writ petition.
3. Brief facts of the case are that the writ
petitioner/appellant is working as peon with Animal
Husbandry Department since 9.6.1993. His date of
birth is 3.8.1972 (as such his age is over 40 years).
Uttarakhand Animal Husbandry Department Livestock
Extension and Poultry Development Service Rules,
2009 are the rules which govern the recruitment to the

2
various categories of posts in the department. For the
post of Livestock Extension Officer, Rule 5 thereof
provides that 85 per cent posts shall be filled up by
direct recruitment, 10 per cent posts shall be filled up
by direct recruitment from amongst substantively
appointed departmental candidates and remaining 5
per cent posts are to be filled from amongst the retired
Veterinary Dressers with prior sanction of the
Government.
4. The advertisement, in question, in response
to which the writ petitioner/appellant appears to have
applied, is the advertisement for the direct recruitment
of the Livestock Extension Officers. No doubt,
departmental employees may also apply and compete
for the post of Livestock Extension Officer in response
to the said advertisement, but they must fulfill the
essential qualifications prescribed for the candidates of
direct recruitment. Condition No. 5, mentioned in the
advertisement in question, shows that on 1st of
January 2013, the maximum age of the candidate
(residents of Uttarakhand), must not exceed 40 years.
Only the reserved category candidates, belonging to
State of Uttarakhand, are entitled to relaxation in age
as per the relevant Government Orders.
5. It is not the case the writ
petitioner/appellant that he belongs to any of the
reserved categories mentioned in the said
advertisement. The ground taken by the writ
petitioner/appellant in the writ petition is that he is
entitled to age relaxation of 5 years in terms of the
Government Order/letter No. 110/Aa.Sa.Pa-Dairy/2005 dated 22.6.2005. Said Government

3
Order/letter stood superceded by Uttarakhand Animal
Husbandry Department Livestock Extension and
Poultry Development Service Rules, 2009. Apart from
this, on perusal of the Government Order/letter dated
22.6.2005, it appears that when the maximum age of
28 years was provided for the candidates appearing for
appointment through direct recruitment for the post of
Livestock Extension Officer, the departmental
candidates were entitled to age relaxation of five years,
but the said order/letter issued by the Government
cannot be read in piecemeal.
6. In the above circumstances, we do not find
any illegality in the impugned order dated 22.3.2013,
passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court, in
Writ Petition No. 307/2013 (S/S), whereby the writ
petition was dismissed.
7. Consequently, this appeal is dismissed
summarily.
 (Stay application no. 3246/2013 also stands
disposed of.)
(Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) (Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
 6.4.2013 6.4.2013
Prabodh
